JaLi's Multi-Language ToolKit ("MLTK") for Excel - Documentation

The MLTK Date Toolkit provides powerful, locale‑aware date formatting functions for Excel. It supports custom formats, literals, escape sequences, capitalization overrides, ordinal switches, and multiple languages.

1. Main Function: MLTK.FORMATDATE()

Syntax:

=MLTK.FORMATDATE(date, lang, formatType, customFormat)

Arguments:

  • date — A Temporal date, ISO string, or Excel serial number.
  • lang — A locale code (e.g., en-US, fr-CA, es-ES).
  • formatType — "short", "long", or "custom".
  • customFormat — Required when formatType="custom".

Example:

=MLTK.FORMATDATE(A2, "fr-CA", "custom", "DDDD, D*/oa MMMM YYYY")
→ lundi, 2e juillet 1990

2. Custom Format Tokens

The following tokens can be used inside a custom format string.

TokenDescriptionExample
YYYY4‑digit year1990
YY2‑digit year90
MMMMFull month nameJuly
MMMShort month nameJul
MMMonth (2 digits)07
MMonth (1–2 digits)7
DDDDFull weekday nameMonday
DDDShort weekday nameMon
DDDay (2 digits)02
DDay (1–2 digits)2
DDORDDay with ordinal (locale rules)2nd
D_ODay + ordinal (only if locale allows)2nd (en-US), 2 (fr-CA)
D_OADay + ordinal (always)2nd (en-US), 2e (fr-CA)
CMMMCapitalized full monthJuillet → Juillet
CMMCapitalized short monthjuil. → Juil.
CdddCapitalized full weekdaylundi → Lundi
CddCapitalized short weekdaylun. → Lun.

3. Literals

Anything inside single quotes is treated as literal text.

DD 'de' MMMM 'de' YYYY
→ 12 de julio de 1990

Use this for Spanish, French, or any language requiring fixed text.

4. Escape Sequences

Anything inside square brackets is literal text.

MMMM [Q] YYYY
→ July Q 1990

Useful for adding symbols or fixed markers.

5. Ordinal Switches

Two switches can be applied after a single D token:

SwitchMeaningExample
D*/oAppend ordinal only if locale allows2 → 2nd (en-US), 2 (fr-CA)
D*/oaAppend ordinal to all numbers if locale allows2 → 2nd (en-US), 2e (fr-CA)

These are normalized internally to D_O and D_OA.

6. Format Normalization

The toolkit automatically corrects common user mistakes:

  • mmmm → MMMM
  • mmm → MMM
  • DDDD → dddd
  • DDD → ddd
  • d*/oa → D_OA
  • d*/o → D_O

Future versions may display warnings in the taskpane.

7. Supported Locales

The toolkit supports a wide range of language tags, including:

fr, fr-CA, fr-FR, en-US, en-GB, en-CA, es-ES, es-MX, de-DE, it-IT, pt-BR, pt-PT

If a locale is not found, en-US is used as fallback.

8. Examples

French (Canada)

DDDD, D*/oa MMMM YYYY
→ lundi, 2e juillet 1990

English (US)

MMMM DD, YYYY
→ July 02, 1990

Spanish (Spain)

DD 'de' MMMM 'de' YYYY
→ 12 de julio de 1990

9. Error Handling

The toolkit validates:

  • unmatched quotes
  • unmatched brackets
  • invalid tokens
  • unknown locale codes

Invalid formats produce a clear error message.

10. Helper Functions

The toolkit includes helper functions for advanced users:

  • MLTK.GetMonthName(date, lang)
  • MLTK.GetMonthAbbrev(date, lang)
  • MLTK.GetDayName(date, lang)
  • MLTK.GetDayAbbrev(date, lang)
  • MLTK.GetOrdinal(day, lang)

These functions are used internally but can also be called directly.

11. Notes

This toolkit is designed to be:

  • locale‑aware
  • collision‑free
  • fully validated
  • Excel‑friendly
  • Temporal‑compatible

It is ideal for multilingual reporting, dashboards, and professional documents.
